I've done a bit of this - here's some of the things I've learned:

  • Many cars have a back seat that flips down and gives you direct access to the trunk, from inside the car. You can use this to get some extra leg room, or if you find it comfortable enough, sleep completely in the trunk and the vehicle just looks empty.
  • 24 hour establishments are usually fine with you using their parking lot during the empty night hours, especially if you make a habit of spending money there. Walmart is a notable example, and if you look it's common for campers and RVs to post up in Walmart lots.
  • In the winter I broke my nights up into two parts: sleep a few hours, wake up at 1AM when it's cold as balls, go buy a hot drink and spend an hour in a heated building warming up, then sleep again.
  • YMCA and coin laundromats are really useful, both as a place to wash and as a place you can park or warm up.
  • A 100W power inverter is cheap and nice if there's something you really want to run from your car. Be careful with laptops though, make sure the inverter can handle their max wattage or it will cut out.
